item.title: ChatGPT Lockdown Bypass and CVE-2026-109518 APT Package-Swap Risk
item.content:encoded:
Window: 05 Nov 11:00 → 05 Nov 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

CVE-2026-109518: apt Flaw Lets Attackers Swap Packages After Verification and Run Code as Root — Should Read

CVE-2026-109518 lets an on-path attacker abuse APT download retries to replace a package after its signature and hash verification, resulting in root code execution. Update APT immediately and disable Acquire::Retries during the upgrade, especially on Debian 12+/Ubuntu 22.04+ CI runners, build images, and systems using HTTP mirrors or proxies.

  • CVE-2026-109518 is an APT flaw that can let an attacker who tampers with HTTP package traffic replace a package after APT verifies its hash and run code as root during installation.
  • The issue affects Debian 12 and later and Ubuntu 22.04 and later by default because APT retries failed downloads three times, while older releases are exposed when Acquire::Retries is set above zero.
  • Debian and Ubuntu released fixed APT versions, including 2.6.2 for Debian 12, 3.0.4 for Debian 13, 2.4.15ubuntu0.1 for Ubuntu 22.04, and 2.8.4ubuntu0.1 for Ubuntu 24.04.
  • Self-hosted CI runners, Docker builds, developer machines, package mirrors, and GitHub-hosted runners can be exposed when an attacker can control package responses and vulnerable APT retries are enabled.
  • The article recommends disabling APT retries with Acquire::Retries=0 before upgrading APT, then rebuilding runner and container images from patched versions.

Technologies: ci-cd, container-platform, network-monitoring, package-registry

Products: apt, github-actions, docker, harden-runner

Vendors: debian, canonical, github, docker, stepsecurity

ChatGPT Lockdown Mode Bypass: Phishing, Malware Delivery, and Silent Data Exfiltration — Should Read

Check Point Research found that ChatGPT’s HTML preview sandbox could bypass Lockdown Mode by abusing popup permissions, enabling phishing, malware delivery, and potentially silent chat-data exfiltration in the ChatGPT Classic app. OpenAI fixed the issue by removing the permissive popup sandbox settings.

  • Check Point Research found that ChatGPT’s HTML page preview feature could be used to bypass Lockdown Mode and open pop-up windows without the intended protections.
  • The issue stemmed from permissive popup settings in nested HTML preview frames, allowing a newly created inner frame to open an unsandboxed pop-up window.
  • The flaw could enable phishing pages, malware-download lures, and exfiltration of chat history or uploaded files through malicious prompts, GPTs, or shared chats.
  • In the Electron-based ChatGPT Classic application, the researchers reported that pop-ups could be opened without a user click, enabling silent chat-data exfiltration during a conversation.
  • OpenAI told the researchers it fixed the issue by removing the allow-popups and allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox permissions from the outer HTML-preview frame.

Products: chatgpt, chatgpt-classic, chatgpt-lockdown-mode, canvas, deep-research, agent-mode

Vendors: openai, check-point

Why the Same Vulnerability Creates Different Risk in Different Plants — Optional

The same OT vulnerability can pose radically different risk across plants depending on reachability, network segmentation, compensating controls, asset criticality, and process consequences. Radiflow argues that organisations should prioritize mitigations based on site-specific attack paths and business impact rather than CVSS severity alone.

  • A CVSS score measures the severity of a vulnerability in the abstract but does not account for a specific industrial site's network design, controls, asset role, or process consequences.
  • OT risk depends on reachability, attack-path length, compensating controls, asset criticality, and the realistic consequences if a device is compromised.
  • In the article's example, a CVSS 9.8 controller flaw is high risk at a wind farm with flat networking and vendor remote access but low risk at an automotive plant where the controller is isolated, its web service is disabled, and a spare unit is available.
  • A risk-based OT program models assets, network zones and connections, analyzes likely routes to critical systems, and links devices to the business processes they support.
  • Radiflow CIARA uses asset and network data to model sites, simulate attack paths, calculate risk by site and zone, and rank mitigations by the risk reduction they provide relative to cost.

Technologies: ics-scada, ids-ips, network-monitoring

Products: ciara, isid, isap, icen

Vendors: radiflow

Is Your Exposure Management Platform Leaving You Exposed? Five Tests to Find Out — Optional

Check Point argues that effective exposure management must unify asset discovery, risk-based prioritization, validation, safe remediation, and verification rather than simply generate vulnerability tickets. The article promotes Check Point Exposure Management as a platform for connecting internal and external asset intelligence to actionable, confirmed protections.

  • The article states that exposure management should connect discovery of a security issue to clear prioritization, an appropriate response, and evidence that protection improved.
  • It describes five evaluation tests: building an accurate asset view, explaining which exposures need action first, validating the exposure and response, carrying remediation through existing workflows, and showing what changed or remains unresolved.
  • The article says CAASM can connect records from cloud platforms, endpoint tools, and inventories to identify stale information, missing ownership, and gaps in security coverage.
  • It says prioritization should consider attacker reachability, exploitability, current threat activity, business impact, and protections already in place.
  • The article argues that completed actions require verification because patches, policy updates, and takedown requests may not fully resolve the original exposure.

Technologies: ids-ips

Products: check-point-exposure-management

Vendors: check-point, cyberint

item.title: Storm-2603 SharePoint Exploits, ARTEX Backdoor, and Zyxel Root-RCE Risks
item.content:encoded:
Window: 05 Nov 07:00 → 05 Nov 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

Zyxel GS1900 Patch Fails to Block Zero-Day Exploit Allowing Root Command Execution — Must Read

Zyxel GS1900 switches remain vulnerable to unauthenticated root command execution even after the earlier Patch 2 update; affected owners must install model-specific 2.90 Patch 3 firmware. The flaw, CVE-2026-107441, was already used in attacks that harvested switch configurations and hashed root credentials.

  • Zyxel’s earlier GS1900 2.90 Patch 2 firmware did not block an exploit that lets an unauthenticated person who can reach the web management interface execute commands with root privileges.
  • Zyxel released 2.90 Patch 3 firmware for 10 GS1900 switch models to address CVE-2026-107441, which affects Patch 2 and earlier firmware.
  • Binarly reported that the exploit uses an oversized request parameter to write beyond an allocated memory area and alter which function the switch’s web-request program calls.
  • GreyNoise reported that attackers collected data from 996 GS1900 switches around August 17, including switch configurations, hashed root credentials, and network information.
  • CISA added CVE-2026-7273 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on September 21, but CVE-2026-107441 was not listed in the catalog data cited by the article.

Technologies: switch

Products: zyxel-gs1900

Vendors: zyxel, binarly, greynoise

CERT-In Flags AI-Driven Attacks as Backdoored ARTEX Exposes 62 Consoles to Root Access — Must Read

CERT-In warns that AI-assisted actors, including Crafty Falcon, are targeting India’s financial sector with automated attacks to steal API credentials and move funds. Separately, a backdoored ARTEX Docker image exposed at least 62 internet-facing consoles to an unauthenticated root shell, highlighting supply-chain risks from unvetted offensive-security tools.

  • CERT-In said the AI-assisted threat actor Crafty Falcon is actively targeting Indian banking, financial services, insurance, cryptocurrency exchanges, and digital asset service providers using tools including ARTEX, PentAGI, Cairn, and CyberStrikeAI.
  • The campaigns exploit internet-facing applications, exposed APIs, privileged endpoints, stolen API tokens, plaintext credentials, and services without multi-factor authentication to obtain credentials and conduct unauthorized fund transfers.
  • CERT-In reported that attackers perform small test transactions, abuse payment-aggregator merchant settlement APIs, deploy malicious code to cloud infrastructure, and delete logs or tamper with endpoint security tools to hinder detection.
  • A copied ARTEX version configured to pull the tomicdd/artex Docker image contains a hidden login routine that lets an unauthenticated requester run commands as root.
  • Researchers found 62 internet-facing ARTEX consoles serving the backdoored build between November 2 and 4, 2026, while Docker Hub reported 9,000 downloads of the tomicdd/artex image.

Technologies: container-platform, source-control, package-registry

Products: artex, docker-hub, github

Vendors: docker, github, microsoft

The SOC Files 5: Ghost in the pipeline, or a fileless SharePoint breach by Storm-2603 — Should Read

Storm-2603 exploited ToolShell flaws in on-premises Microsoft SharePoint to implant a fileless webshell inside IIS w3wp.exe, enabling covert tunneling, privilege escalation, and attempted Warlock ransomware deployment. Defenders should treat SharePoint RCE as a host-level incident and hunt runtime and memory artifacts, anomalous IIS behavior, and post-compromise remote-access tooling—not just files or known IOCs.

  • Storm-2603 activity exploited CVE-2025-53770 and CVE-2025-53771 in on-premises Microsoft SharePoint to achieve remote code execution through crafted HTTP requests.
  • In the analyzed intrusion, attackers injected a fileless webshell into the IIS worker process, w3wp.exe, where it remained in memory until the application pool recycled or IIS restarted.
  • The webshell used a custom VirtualPathProvider and a User-Agent-triggered command channel to proxy TCP traffic to arbitrary hosts inside the victim network.
  • After compromising the server, the attackers installed Velociraptor and deployed several tunneling mechanisms, including Zoho Assist, VS Code CLI tunneling, Cloudflare Tunnel, and a reverse proxy utility.
  • The attackers attempted to deploy Warlock ransomware, but Kaspersky Endpoint Security's Proactive Defense Module blocked the ransomware process.

Technologies: web-server, edr, remote-access, proxy, cloud-platform, object-storage

Products: microsoft-sharepoint, microsoft-iis, kaspersky-endpoint-security, velociraptor, cloudflare-tunnel, zoho-assist, visual-studio-code, supabase-storage, safing-privacy-network

Vendors: microsoft, kaspersky, rapid7, cloudflare, zoho, supabase, safing

GhostMap: The Android flaw that crashes your phone before you open the app — Should Read

Bitdefender researchers disclosed GhostMap, an Android 10+ ZIP/APK parsing flaw that can let a specially crafted app crash system_server repeatedly after installation—even without being opened or granted permissions—potentially forcing a factory reset. The issue stems from inconsistent handling of unsupported ZIP compression methods and declared file sizes, and Google reportedly has not issued a security fix.

  • Bitdefender researchers found that a specially crafted APK can trigger a persistent Android crash loop after installation without being opened, requesting permissions, or containing executable code.
  • The GhostMap flaw arises because Android libraries handle unsupported ZIP compression methods differently, allowing an APK entry’s declared uncompressed size to exceed the actual file data and causing a SIGBUS crash when it is read.
  • Bitdefender reproduced the persistent crash loop on a Pixel 10 running Android 17 with the August 5, 2026 security patch and reported reproductions on Android 10 and later.
  • The crash can affect system_server, causing Android to restart the process and parse the malicious resource again, while safe mode does not stop the loop and recovery may require a factory reset.
  • Google reportedly classified the finding as outside the scope of a security update, referred it to a feature team for possible future consideration, and had not provided a fix as of the article’s publication.

Technologies: mobile-os, antivirus

Products: android, pixel-10, bitdefender-mobile-security, libziparchive, libandroidfw

Vendors: google, bitdefender, android-open-source-project

Apple to Start Scanning Publicly Shared iCloud Photos and Files for Harmful Content — Should Read

Apple will begin scanning iCloud Photos and iCloud Drive items shared publicly via “Anyone with the Link” starting with its 27.3 OS releases, and such links will disable end-to-end encryption even when Advanced Data Protection is enabled.

  • Apple plans to check iCloud Photos and iCloud Drive items shared through the “Anyone with the Link” option for harmful content starting with iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, macOS 27.3, and visionOS 27.3.
  • Content shared using an “Anyone with the Link” iCloud link is accessible to anyone with the link, including Apple.
  • Using “Anyone with the Link” disables end-to-end encryption for the shared item even when Advanced Data Protection is enabled for the owner or recipients.
  • Apple says it may remove harmful content and may block or disable an associated Apple Account, prevent creation of a new account using its email address or phone number, or involve law enforcement when necessary.
  • Apple has not specified what it considers harmful content or whether the checks will apply to previously generated public links.

Technologies: cloud-platform, object-storage, mobile-os, operating-system

Products: icloud, icloud-photos, icloud-drive, advanced-data-protection, ios, ipados, macos, visionos

Vendors: apple

AI-Powered Ransomware Is Coming for UK Critical Infrastructure, and Europe Is Already the Testing Ground — Optional

The UK NCSC warns that AI-assisted ransomware is highly likely to target UK critical national infrastructure by 2028, accelerating familiar entry methods such as unpatched internet-facing systems, phishing, and compromised accounts. European attacks linked to Russian and China-aligned actors show the threat is already developing, making rapid patching, OT segmentation, resilient recovery, and stronger threat intelligence urgent priorities.

  • The UK National Cyber Security Centre assesses that AI-powered malware will highly likely be used in a ransomware attack against UK critical national infrastructure by the end of 2028.
  • UK and EU member states attributed a December 2025 attempted attack on Poland’s energy grid to Russia’s FSB Centre 16, and the attack could have disrupted power for roughly 500,000 people if successful.
  • The NCSC says AI is likely to make established attacker activities, including reconnaissance, social engineering, vulnerability discovery, and exploit development, faster and larger rather than create entirely new attack methods.
  • For large organizations, 88% of incidents handled by the NCSC began through exploiting public-facing applications, phishing, misuse of valid accounts, or exploitation of external remote services.
  • The NCSC recommends that critical infrastructure operators prioritize patching internet-facing systems, separating corporate IT from operational technology, governing internal AI use, rehearsing recovery, and securing their supply chains.

Products: cyble-hawk

Vendors: cyble

5 Active Cyber Threats That Put US Enterprises at Risk in October 2026 — Optional

US enterprises face active phishing and malware campaigns that abuse Microsoft 365 device-code authentication, trusted services, fake AI software, and security-tool evasion to steal tokens, credentials, and data. Organizations should tightly control device-code flows and software installation while monitoring suspicious authentication, PowerShell, Defender, and firewall activity.

  • SkyW4lker and Mir0Auth phishing kits abuse Microsoft’s legitimate device-code authentication flow to obtain access to Microsoft 365 accounts without stealing passwords or bypassing multi-factor authentication.
  • Fake AI campaigns impersonating services such as ChatGPT and Claude use fraudulent downloads and event invitations to distribute malware or steal Microsoft 365 and Google account access.
  • GeorgeGinx uses legitimate Adobe Shared Links to redirect targets in U.S. government, banking, health care, and IT organizations to Microsoft device-code phishing pages.
  • WKLP is a Python-based information stealer and remote-access tool that uses PowerShell and a legitimate Python runtime, adds Microsoft Defender exclusions, terminates security processes, and creates disguised firewall rules.
  • The article says these campaigns can lead to financial losses, data theft, unauthorized account access, and operational disruption for affected enterprises.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, mfa, antivirus

Products: any-run-interactive-sandbox, any-run-threat-intelligence-feeds, microsoft-365, microsoft-entra-conditional-access, microsoft-defender, adobe-shared-links, chatgpt, claude

Vendors: any-run, microsoft, adobe, openai, anthropic

item.title: CISA Flags Actively Exploited Apple CVE-2024-27834 as OpenAI Scales Linux Exploit Generation
item.content:encoded:
Window: 05 Nov 03:00 → 05 Nov 07:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers Exploit Patched Apple Flaw to Deliver Info-Stealing Malware, CISA Says — Must Read

CISA added Apple CVE-2024-27834 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after suspected APT29 activity used patched Safari and Chrome flaws to deliver browser-data-stealing malware. Organizations and users should apply Apple security updates promptly, with U.S. federal agencies directed to remediate by November 18, 2026.

  • CISA added Apple vulnerability CVE-2024-27834 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after reports of active exploitation.
  • CVE-2024-27834 is an improper-authentication flaw that can let an attacker with arbitrary read and write capability bypass Pointer Authentication.
  • Apple addressed the flaw in May 2024 across iOS, iPadOS, macOS Sonoma, tvOS, watchOS, and Safari updates.
  • Sekoia reported that actors possibly linked to Russia, attributed to APT29 with moderate to high confidence, exploited patched Safari and Google Chrome flaws to deliver browser and device data-stealing malware.
  • CISA recommended that U.S. federal civilian agencies apply the necessary patches by November 18, 2026.

Technologies: browser, mobile-os, operating-system

Products: ios, ipados, macos-sonoma, tvos, watchos, safari, google-chrome, webkit, plerdy-seo-tracker

Vendors: apple, google, plerdy

OpenAI AI Pipeline Generates 948 Linux Root Escalation Exploits in 30-Hour Run — Should Read

OpenAI says an agentic pipeline using an upcoming cyber model reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel flaws and generated 948 working local privilege-escalation exploits in a 30-hour run, while also producing patches for human review. The result underscores that AI is accelerating both vulnerability weaponization and defensive patching, shrinking the time organizations have to remediate exposed systems.

  • OpenAI said its prototype analyzed 2,308 Linux kernel candidates, dynamically reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities, and generated 948 local privilege-escalation exploits that could allow an unprivileged local user to obtain root access.
  • The agentic pipeline includes vulnerability discovery, sandboxed dynamic validation, exploitability assessment, patch generation, and human review before reporting findings to maintainers.
  • OpenAI said a mid-October 2026 run completed the validation work within 30 hours and cost $1,213,430 in API credits, or about $1,279 per local privilege-escalation exploit.
  • OpenAI said the agents discovered and used at least 10 novel Linux exploitation techniques, including kernel-cache object spraying, page grooming, data-only privilege escalation, and arbitrary type confusion.
  • The U.K. National Cyber Security Centre said AI-powered cyber tools have increased zero-day discovery and shortened patching timelines, while organizations must adapt their patching and testing processes to the faster pace.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: gpt-5-5-cyber, linux-kernel

Vendors: openai, linux-kernel-project

item.title: Netskope CASB Adds Deferred Policy Actions and Automated Incident Resolution
item.content:encoded:

Give People a Deadline, Then Let Fixed Incidents Close Themselves — Optional

Netskope One CASB API adds Deferred Policy Action to give file owners time to remediate violations before restrictions are enforced, and Automated Incident Remediation Tracking to automatically mark corrected incidents as Auto Resolved. Together, the features reduce manual incident review and provide clearer reporting on remediation outcomes.

  • Netskope One CASB API now offers Deferred Policy Action, which first alerts a file owner and applies a restrictive action only if the violation remains after a set number of days.
  • Administrators configure Deferred Policy Action by selecting Set Time Trigger, choosing notification recipients and an email template, setting a remediation period, and defining the follow-up action.
  • Automated Incident Remediation Tracking monitors files that triggered incidents and changes the status to Auto Resolved when the file no longer matches the policy.
  • The article states that automatically resolving fixed incidents reduces manual review work and makes open queues more focused on exposures that still remain.
  • Immediate restrictive action remains recommended when an organization cannot tolerate several days of exposure, while a time trigger can suit external-sharing policies that owners can fix themselves.

item.title: Amadeus Airline Breaches, Zyxel Zero-Day Exploitation, and Stolen-Session Defenses
item.content:encoded:
Window: 04 Nov 19:00 → 04 Nov 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

Zyxel fixes zero-day exploited to hack nearly 1,000 network switches — Must Read

Zyxel patched CVE-2026-107441, an actively exploited unauthenticated remote command-execution flaw in GS1900 switches that attackers used to compromise nearly 1,000 devices and steal configurations and credentials. Administrators should install the latest firmware, as prior patches for CVE-2026-7273 did not stop this separate zero-day.

  • Zyxel released firmware updates on October 22 for CVE-2026-107441, an unauthenticated flaw in GS1900 switch web management interfaces that can let network-accessible attackers run operating-system commands.
  • GreyNoise reported that the Kapibala threat actor compromised 996 Zyxel devices across 48 countries beginning around August 17, 2026.
  • Attackers used the exploited flaw to run commands and download a script that collected device configurations, hashed root credentials, and network information.
  • The attacks were initially attributed to CVE-2026-7273, but Binarly determined that the exploit targeted the separate, previously unknown CVE-2026-107441.
  • Zyxel's latest firmware limits HTTP parameter sizes and checks the parameter count before copying data into memory, blocking the exploitation method described by Binarly.

Technologies: switch

Products: gs1900

Vendors: zyxel

More Asian airlines announce data breaches after attack on Spanish IT provider Amadeus — Should Read

A vulnerability in Amadeus’s travel booking display environment exposed customer booking data for multiple Asian airlines, affecting at least 191,000 records across Japan Airlines, Cathay Pacific, and Singapore Airlines. Exposed data included passenger names, booking references, itineraries, and in some cases passport or travel-document details, though Amadeus says no payment data was accessed.

  • Multiple Asian airlines reported customer-data breaches linked to a vulnerability in an Amadeus travel booking display environment.
  • Amadeus said certain booking-display data was accessible through the vulnerability and that it found no evidence that payment or financial data was accessed.
  • Japan Airlines said information belonging to 92,000 customers was stolen, Singapore Airlines said 46,000 records were accessed, and Cathay Pacific said 53,000 records were stolen.
  • Cathay Pacific said the exposed data included booking numbers, passenger names, and flight details, while some records also contained passports or other travel documents, frequent-flyer numbers, and email addresses.
  • Amadeus said it fixed the vulnerability and added enhanced monitoring and detection capabilities, while the affected airlines said their own systems and operations were not impacted.

Vendors: amadeus

DreamHost confirms data breach exposed FTP logins and webmail sessions — Should Read

DreamHost says attackers exploited its web-based File Manager from August through October 23, 2026, exposing FTP/SFTP credentials and potentially some webmail session data. The company reset affected passwords and sessions, patched the flaw, and says billing and control-panel credentials were not accessed.

  • DreamHost said an unauthorized party accessed the server running its web-based File Manager at files.dreamhost.com from approximately August 2026 through October 23, 2026.
  • The intruder exploited a software flaw to access FTP/SFTP usernames and passwords for people who logged into the File Manager during that period.
  • DreamHost said a limited number of users may also have had webmail session information, including credentials, accessed.
  • The company said it found no evidence that control panel login information or customer billing and payment details were accessed.
  • DreamHost said it blocked the intruder, fixed the exploited flaw, ended potentially affected active sessions, and invalidated passwords.

Products: dreamhost-file-manager, dreamhost-webmail

Vendors: dreamhost, equifax

Vercel rolls out new protection against stolen session cookie attacks — May Read

Vercel is gradually deploying Device Bound Session Credentials, which bind login sessions to TPM-protected device keys so stolen cookies cannot be reused on another device. It also launched Security Review in public beta to scan GitHub code changes for issues such as exposed secrets and missing authorization checks.

  • Vercel is gradually rolling out Device Bound Session Credentials for vercel.com logins, tying sessions to a private key stored in a user device’s TPM.
  • The feature is intended to prevent stolen session cookies from being reused on another device, and currently works in Chrome on macOS and Windows.
  • Vercel is also rolling out DPoP, a similar protective technology, for its Vercel CLI.
  • Vercel launched Security Review in public beta for Pro and Enterprise teams, using Vercel Agent to scan code changes on pushes to connected GitHub repositories.
  • Security Review can flag missing authorization checks and exposed secrets, and Vercel says scans are free until November 10, 2026 while agent-generated fixes are billed separately.

Technologies: cloud-platform, browser, source-control, identity-provider

Products: vercel, vercel-cli, security-review, vercel-agent, next-js, google-chrome, google-workspace

Vendors: vercel, google, github

Canadian extradited to US for allegedly hacking schools in at least four states — May Read

A Canadian man was extradited to the U.S. to face charges that he and another Canadian allegedly hacked educational institutions in four states from 2016 to 2019, stealing credentials and installing cryptomining software. U.S. authorities are still seeking the co-defendant’s extradition from Canada.

  • The U.S. Department of Justice charged Canadian nationals Ryan James Roach and Mathiew James Stubbings over an alleged 2016–2019 campaign targeting educational institutions.
  • Roach was arrested in Canada, extradited to the United States, and appeared in federal court in Rochester, New York, while U.S. authorities are still pursuing Stubbings’ extradition.
  • Prosecutors allege the pair stole login credentials, used servers in several European countries to conceal their identities, and installed cryptocurrency-mining software on compromised computers.
  • The alleged targets included educational institutions in New York, Tennessee, North Carolina, and Massachusetts, particularly those with supercomputers.
  • Both defendants face charges carrying a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison.

Surviving cybersecurity until the end of 2026 — Optional

Organizations should assume that developer laptops, vendors, packages, and CI systems will eventually be compromised, then limit the damage through short-lived credentials, tight access controls, dependency and vendor hygiene, reduced internet exposure, and continuous testing.

  • Recent incidents involving a developer laptop, compromised PyPI packages, PHP2Shell, Node2Shell, and eMudhra demonstrate that familiar techniques can cause severe damage and that exploitation can follow disclosures quickly.
  • Organizations should assume that a laptop, vendor, package, or CI runner will eventually be compromised and focus on limiting how far an attacker can move from that initial compromise.
  • Short-lived credentials, tightly limited permissions, multi-factor authentication, and regular credential audits can reduce the impact of stolen tokens and keys.
  • Teams should track and patch open-source dependencies, use minimal and hardened container images where appropriate, and remove unsupported or unused software.
  • Organizations should inventory their internet-exposed services and vendors, remove unnecessary access and integrations, control software installed on user machines, and routinely test their defenses through attack-surface monitoring, network testing, and breach exercises.

Technologies: package-registry, source-control, container-platform, orchestration, ci-cd

item.title: APT Root Flaw, France Refrigeration Attack, and Google Calendar Session Phishing
item.content:encoded:
Window: 04 Nov 15:00 → 04 Nov 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

Debian and Ubuntu APT Flaw Lets MitM Attackers Swap Verified Packages and Run Code as Root — Should Read

A critical APT flaw, CVE-2026-109518, lets man-in-the-middle attackers who can alter HTTP package traffic abuse download retries to replace verified Debian or Ubuntu packages with malicious code that executes as root. Debian and Ubuntu have issued APT updates, and systems using default retry settings on Debian 12 or Ubuntu 22.04 and later are particularly exposed.

  • CVE-2026-109518 is a critical APT flaw that can allow an attacker who modifies package-download traffic to swap a checked package for a malicious one and run code as root.
  • The attack relies on APT retrying failed downloads, which is enabled by default in Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 and later.
  • An attacker can use HTTP redirects and temporary server errors to trigger retries when a system installs a package.
  • Debian has released fixed APT versions, while Ubuntu published updated APT builds for Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, 24.04 LTS, 26.04 LTS, and 26.10.
  • Older releases such as Debian 11 and Ubuntu 20.04 are not exposed by default, but may be affected if the Acquire::Retries setting was enabled.

Technologies: operating-system, package-registry

Products: apt, debian, ubuntu

Vendors: debian, ubuntu, apt

SonicWall Won't Patch EoL GMS Flaws That Could Expose Files, Alter Database Records — Should Read

SonicWall will not patch two serious vulnerabilities in end-of-life Global Management System (GMS) versions 9.5.2 and earlier, including an unauthenticated file-read flaw and a post-authentication SQL injection issue. Organizations are urged to migrate to SonicWall Network Security Manager (NSM).

  • SonicWall disclosed two vulnerabilities affecting end-of-life Global Management System (GMS) version 9.5.2 and earlier, and said it will not release fixes for them.
  • CVE-2026-109593 has a CVSS score of 9.1 and could let an unauthenticated network-based attacker read internal GMS files.
  • CVE-2026-109594 has a CVSS score of 6.8 and could allow an authenticated attacker, under specific conditions, to access or modify information in the GMS database through SQL injection.
  • SonicWall strongly recommends that organizations using GMS upgrade to SonicWall Network Security Manager (NSM).
  • The article also notes active exploitation of the separate SonicWall CVE-2026-102255 SSRF flaw, with Previdian recording 2,541 attempts from eight IP addresses since October 9, 2026.

Technologies: remote-access

Products: global-management-system-gms, network-security-manager-nsm, sma-1000

Vendors: sonicwall

Cyberattack disrupts blood storage refrigeration systems in France — Should Read

A cyberattack on a refrigeration supplier altered temperature and defrost settings at three French Blood Establishment facilities, putting stored blood products at risk. Monitoring systems enabled staff to secure or transfer the products, with no reported losses or disruption to blood services.

  • A cyberattack on November 2 affected remote monitoring and control systems for refrigeration equipment at three French Blood Establishment facilities, raising temperature and defrost thresholds in cold-storage chambers.
  • The French Blood Establishment said it was not directly targeted; its refrigeration supplier was affected, and Coolworld Rentals confirmed that a third-party component vulnerability affected a limited number of its units.
  • The organization’s monitoring and alarm systems detected the temperature changes, enabling staff to repair affected equipment or transfer blood products and biological samples to other refrigerated facilities.
  • The French Blood Establishment reported no health impact, no loss of blood products, and no interruption to blood collection or distribution.
  • The incident followed attacks on refrigeration systems at supermarkets in France and several other European countries, where temperature settings or defrost functions were remotely altered.

Technologies: ics-scada, iot-device

Products: danfoss-ak-sm, danfoss-ak-sc, danfoss-ak-sm-8xxa, copeland-dixell-xweb

Vendors: coolworld-rentals, danfoss, copeland, dixell

NIKKE PC game launcher hacked to spread remote access, data-stealing malware — Should Read

Hackers tampered with Goddess of Victory: NIKKE’s PC launcher scripts in a supply-chain compromise, potentially deploying a K2F remote-access backdoor and tools to steal browser credentials and cryptocurrency wallet data. Players should update the launcher, scan affected systems, and reset sensitive credentials from a clean device if compromise is suspected.

  • Goddess of Victory: NIKKE developers confirmed that third parties may have tampered with PC launcher script files and issued a client update on November 4 at approximately 02:30 UTC+9.
  • Researcher MotherSphere reported that four JavaScript files on Level Infinite’s official CDN were modified to download additional code from the attacker-controlled insightjs[.]com and insightjs[.]org domains.
  • The downloaded code reportedly used the launcher to execute a LuaJIT payload named insight.bundle that installed a remote-access agent called K2F.
  • K2F could execute commands, access local files, capture screenshots, collect NIKKE account credentials, and steal information stored in web browsers.
  • A malicious Windows DLL associated with the incident contained code to collect cryptocurrency wallet recovery phrases and private keys from browser extensions including MetaMask, Phantom, and Coinbase Wallet.

Technologies: remote-access, browser

Products: goddess-of-victory-nikke, nikke-pc-launcher

Vendors: shift-up, level-infinite

mSecure password manager hack prompts password reset warnings — Should Read

mSeven Software says an attacker stole an encrypted mSecure Cloud customer database and is urging current and former users to change stored passwords, reset MFA, and remove passkeys. Although the company says it has no evidence vault contents were accessed, stolen encrypted vaults may be vulnerable to offline cracking if master passwords were weak.

  • mSeven Software notified current and former mSecure customers of suspicious activity involving the mSecure password-management application.
  • Customers who synchronized their data through mSecure Cloud were reportedly affected after a hacker stole an encrypted database containing information for current and former users.
  • mSeven advised customers to change stored passwords, reset or re-enroll two-factor authentication methods, and remove existing passkeys.
  • The company reportedly said it has no evidence that the attacker accessed confidential information inside the encrypted database.
  • mSecure says its vault data is encrypted locally using AES-256 before being sent to company servers under a zero-knowledge design.

Technologies: secrets-manager

Products: msecure, msecure-cloud

Vendors: mseven-software, lastpass

Google Calendar phishing campaign hijacks sessions, bypasses MFA — Should Read

Material Security says its Operation CloudFire disrupted a phishing campaign that used Google Calendar and Drive lures, trusted Google redirects, and reverse-proxy sign-in pages to steal live Google Workspace sessions and bypass MFA. The campaign relied on compromised sender accounts and rapidly rotated infrastructure, highlighting the need to monitor Workspace sessions and OAuth grants rather than relying solely on link reputation.

  • Since mid-August 2026, a phishing operation has used Google Calendar invitations and later Google Drive file and document-share invitations to target corporate users.
  • The campaign used Google redirect links, Cloudflare Turnstile challenges, and a live reverse proxy of Google’s sign-in page to capture active Google sessions while victims completed real MFA prompts.
  • Captured sessions can provide access to Gmail, Google Drive, and the ability to grant OAuth access in the victim’s name.
  • Material Security’s Operation CloudFire reported malicious gateway and backend URLs to Cloudflare, which applied phishing warning pages to validated destinations.
  • Over one month, Material recorded 68,676 blocked campaign messages, 2,112 malicious URLs analyzed, 897 domains taken down, and 8,570 compromised sender addresses across 6,354 root domains.

Technologies: email-security, cloud-platform, identity-provider, mfa, proxy, waf

Products: google-workspace, google-calendar, google-drive, cloudflare-turnstile, microsoft-365

Vendors: material-security, google, cloudflare, microsoft, intuit

Researchers Uncover Prompt Adware Hidden in OpenAI Codex Jailbreak Toolkit — May Read

Check Point found that the Haiou OpenAI Codex jailbreak bundle persistently alters agent instructions to display ads for a third-party LLM gateway, illustrating a new "prompt adware" supply-chain risk from untrusted AI configurations and skills.

  • Check Point Research identified the Haiou OpenAI Codex jailbreak bundle as "prompt adware" because it modifies an AI agent’s instructions to insert advertisements into later responses.
  • Haiou changes Codex configuration and global instruction files so greetings such as "hi," "hello," and "Seagull" can trigger advertisements for zz.aiapi2025[.]top, an OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway.
  • The bundle uses prompt-injection approaches including role-playing and presenting cybersecurity requests as Capture The Flag scenarios, and it installs skills focused on penetration testing, cracking, and reverse engineering.
  • The haiou-codex GitHub repository presents itself as a local enhancement package for Codex, and the jailbreak is also bundled with the Codex-X graphical configuration tool.
  • Check Point said that third-party prompts, skills, and components can become part of the trust chain as AI agents are adopted in enterprise environments.

Technologies: source-control, api-gateway

Products: openai-codex, haiou-codex, codex-x, zz-aiapi2025-top

Vendors: openai, check-point-research, github

Ukrainian news outlet Kyiv Independent hit by suspected Russian cyberattack — May Read

The Kyiv Independent’s website and newsletter systems were compromised to distribute false Russian- and English-language claims, including fabricated nuclear and physical attacks involving President Zelensky. The outlet suspects Russian actors but has not provided technical attribution evidence and says member and donor payment data was unaffected.

  • The Kyiv Independent said attackers accessed its website management system and newsletter distribution service, enabling them to post false content and email subscribers in Russian and English.
  • One fraudulent Russian-language email falsely claimed that President Volodymyr Zelensky had launched a nuclear warhead at Kyiv after meeting Russian President Vladimir Putin.
  • The publication suspects Russian actors based on the messages’ content but did not provide technical evidence tying the intrusion to Moscow.
  • The Kyiv Independent said members’ and donors’ banking information was not compromised because payments are processed by secure third-party services.
  • Staff are working with cybersecurity specialists to investigate the breach, identify weaknesses, and prevent additional intrusions.

Technologies: cms

Leveraging Microsoft Graph API Change Notifications for Data Exfiltration — May Read

Microsoft Graph Rich Change Notifications can be abused by attackers with compromised user tokens or privileged app permissions to continuously exfiltrate Teams messages and Outlook email previews to attacker-controlled webhooks through Microsoft infrastructure. Organizations should inventory Graph subscriptions and monitor MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs and GraphNotificationsActivityLogs for suspicious subscription creation and activity.

  • Microsoft Graph Change Notifications let users and service principals subscribe to supported Microsoft 365 resources and receive updates at external webhooks or Azure Event Hubs and Event Grids.
  • Rich Notifications can include encrypted resource data, allowing a compromised user with delegated Mail.Read, Mail.ReadWrite, Chat.Read, or Chat.ReadWrite permissions to receive Outlook email previews or Teams message content at an attacker-controlled webhook.
  • Teams message Rich Notifications can return full message bodies, while Outlook message subscriptions allow the bodyPreview property, which is limited to the first 255 characters of an email body.
  • A compromised service principal with the application permission Chat.Read.All can create a Rich Notification subscription for /chats/getAllMessages and receive Teams messages across the organization.
  • Administrators can list tenant subscriptions with Get-MgSubscription and monitor MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs for subscription API activity and GraphNotificationsActivityLogs for triggered notification events.

Technologies: iam, cloud-platform, database, message-queue, secrets-manager

Products: microsoft-graph-api, microsoft-entra-id, microsoft-365, microsoft-teams, microsoft-outlook, azure-functions, azure-cosmos-db, azure-event-hubs, azure-event-grid, azure-key-vault, microsoft-graph-powershell, roadtools, m365permissions

Vendors: microsoft, netspi

Mi Scusi, My SCSI: Abusing iSCSI Target Server — Optional

Windows iSCSI targets configured without CHAP authentication can be accessed by impersonating authorized initiator IQNs, allowing attackers to enumerate and read shared virtual disks. This can expose sensitive clustered workloads such as Hyper-V VM disks and, potentially, Active Directory credential data unless iSCSI is authenticated, segmented, and protected.

  • Windows iSCSI Target Server can be configured to permit initiator connections without CHAP authentication.
  • An unauthenticated iSCSI discovery session can return target names when presented with an initiator name that is listed as authorized.
  • Microsoft iSCSI initiator names are predictably built from a host's DNS name, allowing potential initiator names to be generated from Active Directory or DNS enumeration.
  • An attacker who can impersonate an authorized iSCSI initiator can access shared block storage without NTFS permission checks and may retrieve virtual hard-disk files.
  • The article recommends enabling CHAP, using IPsec where appropriate, and isolating iSCSI storage with network segmentation and host-based firewalls.

Technologies: operating-system, hypervisor, identity-provider

Products: windows-server, windows-iscsi-target-server, hyper-v, active-directory, bloodhound-enterprise, adiskreader, impacket

Vendors: microsoft, specterops, skelsec, fortra

Your AI Agent Has an Owner. Does it Have an Expiration date? — Optional

Health-ISAC leaders warn that AI agents and other non-human identities can become a major healthcare breach risk unless organizations enforce ownership, expiration, vendor oversight, and stronger identity and data governance.

  • Health-ISAC’s Dallas Executive Forum brought together health sector cybersecurity leaders to discuss AI, automation, and identity.
  • Participants said AI is exposing longstanding gaps in identity hygiene, vendor oversight, and data governance rather than creating entirely new problems.
  • The article states that non-human identities can outnumber human users by more than 100 to 1.
  • The forum highlighted the risk that unmanaged AI agents could create agent sprawl and become a critical breach vector for healthcare organizations.

item.title: APT29 Mobile Exploits, Xen VM Escape Flaws, and Beget Data Destruction
item.content:encoded:
Window: 04 Nov 11:00 → 04 Nov 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

APT29-Linked Hackers Hijack Web Analytics Script to Deliver iOS and Android Exploits — Must Read

APT29-linked operators compromised websites, lookalike domains, and Plerdy’s analytics script to profile mobile visitors and deliver DarkSword iOS or AndroSnitch Android exploit chains. The watering-hole campaign can steal browser data, Wi-Fi passwords, and—in some iOS cases—extensive device data from unpatched devices.

  • Sekoia attributed the Poisoned Source watering-hole campaign to the Russia-linked APT29 group and said it targeted iOS and Android users through compromised websites, lookalike domains, and a supply-chain compromise of Plerdy SEO Tracker.
  • Between August 27 and September 3, 2026, malicious code was injected into Plerdy’s a.plerdy[.]com/public/js/click/main.js analytics script, potentially affecting sites that loaded it.
  • The injected JavaScript profiled visitors’ browsers and devices before delivering platform-specific exploit chains for iOS or Android devices.
  • The iOS DarkSword chain could collect cookies or, on targeted iOS 18.5 devices, steal extensive data including messages, passwords, contacts, photos, call history, and data from several Apple services and apps.
  • On Android, the campaign used CVE-2026-3910 and CVE-2025-27038 to deliver AndroSnitch, which collected Chrome data and Wi-Fi passwords without establishing persistence.

Technologies: browser, mobile-os

Products: ios, google-chrome, plerdy-seo-tracker, darksword, coruna, androsnitch

Vendors: apple, google, plerdy

Critical Rails Flaw Lets Attackers Write Server Files via Crafted ImageMagick Uploads — Must Read

Ruby on Rails patched a critical Active Storage flaw (GHSA-f3w6-w445-fwh9) that can let unauthenticated attackers use crafted ImageMagick uploads to write—and, with Disk storage, potentially read—arbitrary server files. Upgrade to Rails 8.1.4.1 or 8.0.5.2, ensure MiniMagick 5.1+ and a restrictive ImageMagick policy are in use, and rotate accessible secrets if Disk-backed uploads may have been exposed.

  • Ruby on Rails disclosed and fixed GHSA-f3w6-w445-fwh9, a critical Active Storage flaw that can allow an unauthenticated attacker to write arbitrary server files through a crafted upload processed by ImageMagick.
  • Applications are affected when they accept untrusted uploads, use ImageMagick through Active Storage’s MiniMagick processor, and do not have an ImageMagick policy that blocks the relevant coders.
  • For applications using Active Storage’s Disk service, the flaw can also allow attackers to read files the application can access, including secrets that could enable remote code execution or access to connected systems.
  • Rails fixed the issue in versions 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2, and applications using MiniMagick must use version 5.1 or later to load the shipped ImageMagick security policy.
  • The releases also address GHSA-v924-7rp8-4mxh, which could let attackers influence the decoder used by ImageMagick or FFmpeg through an uploaded filename and declared content type.

Products: ruby-on-rails, active-storage, imagemagick, mini-magick, graphicsmagick, ffmpeg

Vendors: ruby-on-rails, imagemagick, minimagick, graphicsmagick, ffmpeg

China-Aligned Hackers Hijack Sogou Input Method DNS Requests to Deploy DarkVigil Backdoor — Must Read

China-aligned SlippyNunchucks hijacked insecure DNS/HTTP requests from Tencent’s Sogou Input Method to deliver the DarkVigil backdoor to Chinese-speaking targets across Asia. Tencent patched the issue as CVE-2026-120422 in Sogou Input Method 16.10 by moving the affected requests to HTTPS.

  • ESET attributed a campaign observed from July 1, 2026, to the China-aligned SlippyNunchucks group, which used Sogou Input Method to distribute the DarkVigil backdoor.
  • The attackers altered DNS results for a Sogou configuration domain, causing insecure HTTP requests from the application to reach attacker-controlled servers that supplied a malicious configuration.
  • The malicious configuration instructed a legitimate Sogou component to download a legitimate Adobe executable and a malicious DLL containing DarkVigil, then run the malware through DLL sideloading.
  • ESET reported targets in Hong Kong, Thailand, Japan, Vietnam, Oman, and Sri Lanka, including significant surveillance activity against an organization operating Chinese-language online betting platforms.
  • Tencent addressed CVE-2026-120422 in Sogou Input Method version 16.10 on October 29, 2026, by changing the affected HTTP requests to HTTPS.

Technologies: vpn

Products: sogou-input-method, quickfox, qingtalk, miyunchat, softcam, tawk-to

Vendors: tencent, adobe, quickfox

Xen Hypervisor Flaws Let One Malicious VM Read and Write Any Other VM's Memory — Should Read

Critical Xen grant-copy flaws, CVE-2026-102703 and CVE-2026-102704, let a malicious guest VM read and write other VMs’ memory, potentially compromising dom0 and the entire host. Organizations using Xen 4.6 or later should apply XSA-523 patches and reboot affected hosts; no mitigation is available.

  • Two Xen grant-copy flaws, CVE-2026-102703 and CVE-2026-102704, allow a malicious guest virtual machine to read and write the memory of other virtual machines on the same host, including dom0.
  • The flaws affect Xen versions 4.6 and later, while Xen 4.5 and earlier are not vulnerable.
  • Xen Project released patches under advisory XSA-523 for Xen 4.17 through 4.19 and xen-unstable, but provided no patches for Xen 4.6 through 4.16 and stated there is no known mitigation.
  • XCP-ng warned that a compromised guest could escape its isolation and take over the host, and released an updated Xen package for XCP-ng 8.3 that requires a host reboot.
  • Anthropic found the flaws using its Claude model, with validation by Stephan Lipp of Ada Logics and an independent report by the CodeAnt AI Security Research Team.

Technologies: hypervisor, operating-system

Products: xen, xcp-ng, qubes-os

Vendors: xen-project, anthropic, ada-logics, codeant-ai, vates, qubes-os, debian

Cyberattack wipes cloud data at major Russian hosting provider Beget — Should Read

Russian hosting provider Beget suffered a cyberattack that erased cloud data and virtual-server backups, disrupting hundreds of websites and requiring manual inspection of more than 1,000 servers. File-level backups may allow partial recovery, but the company has not disclosed how the attackers gained access.

  • Beget said attackers accessed systems used to manage its infrastructure and ran scripts that erased data.
  • The attack wiped data tied to Beget's VPS, cloud storage, and Kubernetes services, and the company lost all binary backups of virtual servers while retaining file-level backups.
  • Beget said restoring services would take considerable time because more than 1,000 servers must be manually inspected.
  • The outage disrupted websites and online services in Russia, including the Naryan-Mar city administration website and the Chestny Znak product-labeling system.
  • Beget said it found no evidence that attackers downloaded or altered customer data, but urged customers to change passwords, access keys, and other credentials stored on affected systems.

Technologies: cloud-platform, object-storage, backup, container-platform, orchestration

Products: kubernetes

Vendors: beget

French blood service hit by Europe-wide cyberattacks on refrigeration — Should Read

A Europe-wide cyberattack on third-party refrigeration control systems altered temperature and defrost settings at three French blood-service sites, but EFS said monitoring and rapid transfers prevented any loss or compromise of blood products. The campaign has reportedly affected organizations in at least 11 European countries, with no perpetrators identified.

  • A cyber incident altered temperature and defrost thresholds to very high levels in cold-storage rooms at three Établissement Français du Sang sites in France.
  • EFS said its monitoring and alarm systems detected the anomalies quickly, allowing affected equipment to be controlled or neutralized and stored products to be transferred when necessary.
  • EFS reported that no health impacts or losses of blood products occurred, and that no blood samples or products were compromised.
  • The incident reached EFS through a third-party refrigeration-equipment provider rather than a direct attack on the organization.
  • The latest wave of refrigeration-system incidents has reportedly affected businesses in at least 11 European countries, and no group or entity has claimed responsibility.

Technologies: iot-device

See the agents, set the terms: new visibility and control for personal agents — Optional

Cloudflare launched analytics and granular access policies for personal AI agents, allowing site owners to identify agent traffic and choose whether to allow, limit on ad-supported pages, or block specific agents.

  • Cloudflare added a Personal Assistants category in Security Analytics so site owners can isolate and review traffic from personal agents over time.
  • A new Personal Assistants widget identifies which agents visit a site and lets teams examine their requested paths, response status codes, and originating networks.
  • Cloudflare’s Account Abuse Protection, currently in early access, can show which user a personal agent represents for login and sign-up events.
  • Cloudflare renamed its setting to AI Crawler and Agent access policies and now lets site owners set policies for individual supported personal agents.
  • Supported personal-agent policies include Allow (do not block), Block on pages with ads, and Block.

Technologies: waf

Products: cloudflare-security-analytics, account-abuse-protection, cloudflare-waf, ai-crawler-and-agent-access-policies

Vendors: cloudflare

Radio With No Radar: Why Agent Runtime Security Fails Without the Layers Beneath It — Optional

Agent runtime security cannot rely solely on gateways because many enterprise agents operate inside SaaS platforms beyond gateway visibility; effective enforcement requires continuous discovery, identity and permission context, delegation-chain tracking, and controls at multiple execution points. The article promotes Reco's platform as a way to build that visibility and governance foundation before deploying runtime controls.

  • The article argues that gateway-only agent security cannot observe many AI agents that operate entirely inside third-party platforms such as Salesforce, Slack, Microsoft 365, and Workday.
  • In the cited email incident, an AI assistant offered to send a mass-email batch through an employee's personal mailbox after the approved automation hit a recipient-limit policy.
  • The article says real-time decisions about agent actions require prior knowledge of the agent's owner, permissions, normal behavior, data sensitivity, destination, and delegation chain.
  • It cites a March 2026 compromise of the LiteLLM open-source gateway, with malicious packages reportedly live for about forty minutes and CloudSEK estimating exposure at more than 2,500 organizations.
  • The article recommends that organizations first discover their agents, assign owners, manage configurations and risk, and then add enforcement controls across multiple places where agents operate.

Products: reco-platform, reco-graph, agent360, litellm, claude, slack, microsoft-365-copilot

item.content:encoded:
Window: 04 Nov 07:00 → 04 Nov 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers use n-day exploits in zero-click attacks on iOS, Android devices — Must Read

APT29-linked attackers used compromised and spoofed websites to silently profile iOS and Android visitors and deliver device-specific exploit chains that stole cookies, credentials, messaging data, and other sensitive information. Apple and Google have patched the exploited flaws, so users should install the latest available updates.

  • Sekoia attributed a large-scale watering-hole campaign to APT29 with moderate-to-high confidence, targeting iOS and Android users through compromised websites and lookalike domains.
  • Injected JavaScript profiled visitors’ devices and browser versions, after which a command-and-control server delivered platform-specific exploit chains without requiring user interaction.
  • The iOS exploit chains targeted Safari cookies and, on iOS 18.5, could collect WhatsApp and Telegram databases, Keychain credentials, location data, and photos.
  • The Android chain targeted Chrome versions 139 through 145 except 143 and used AndroSnitch to collect Chrome cookies, login data, browsing history, and saved Wi-Fi credentials.
  • Apple and Google have patched the vulnerabilities used in the campaign, and Sekoia said the payloads did not establish persistence, so rebooting ends the malicious activity until the victim revisits a compromised site.

Technologies: browser, mobile-os

Products: ios, android, safari, chrome, plerdy-seo-tracker, whatsapp, telegram

Vendors: apple, google, sekoia, plerdy

Google Issues Patches for Critical Android Flaw That Could Allow RCE Without User Interaction — Must Read

Google’s November 2026 Android security update fixes CVE-2026-58868, a critical heap buffer overflow affecting Android 14–17 that could enable remote code execution without user interaction. Users should install the 2026-11-01 patch level or later, while the 2026-11-05 level includes all November fixes.

  • Google’s November 2026 Android security bulletin fixes CVE-2026-58868, a critical flaw affecting Android 14 through 17 that could allow remote code execution without user interaction.
  • CVE-2026-58868 is an out-of-bounds write caused by a heap buffer overflow in the onOutputReceived function in FrameDecoder.cpp.
  • Android devices need the 2026-11-01 security patch level or later for fixes covering CVE-2026-58868, while the 2026-11-05 patch level covers every flaw in the November bulletin.
  • Another critical flaw, CVE-2026-58882, could allow a remote denial-of-service attack through Android’s WAP Push SMS message code without user interaction.
  • Google’s November bulletin lists 216 vulnerabilities, including 23 rated Critical, and reported no known exploitation as of November 4.

Products: android, android-runtime, google-play-system-update

UK Cybercrime Journal: Beacon CRM Breach Impacts Over 1,500 Charities — Should Read

Beacon CRM exposed database backups for more than 1,000 UK charities after an AWS access key was leaked in public JavaScript artifacts, putting donor and service-user personal data at risk. The incident underscores the supply-chain impact of poor secret management and overly broad cloud access permissions.

  • Beacon CRM reported that attackers used an AWS access key exposed in publicly accessible JavaScript build artifacts to gain access around 27 July 2026.
  • From 27 to 28 July 2026, the attackers downloaded full database backups containing records from more than 1,000 UK charity customers.
  • The affected backups included names, email addresses, phone numbers, home addresses, donation histories, and uploaded attachments, but did not contain payment card numbers or live bank details.
  • Beacon CRM detected the unauthorised activity on 29 July, revoked the exposed credentials, and began notifying affected organisations between 30 July and 3 August.

Products: beacon-crm, amazon-web-services

Russian Police Arrest 3 Suspected VasyGrek Hackers, Dismantle Criminal Infrastructure — Should Read

Russian police arrested three suspected members of the financially motivated VasyGrek (Fluffy Wolf) hacking group and dismantled infrastructure used to phish organizations and steal funds. The group has targeted organizations across Russia, Belarus, and Kazakhstan using phishing-delivered malware and remote-access tools.

  • Russian authorities arrested three suspected VasyGrek members, searched their residences and offices, and seized computers, communication devices, and other evidence.
  • The Russian Interior Ministry said the group is suspected of stealing funds from organizational accounts and creating, distributing, and using malicious software.

item.content:encoded:

CISA flags WordPress RCE flaw as actively exploited in attacks — Must Read

CISA has added the actively exploited WordPress Core flaw CVE-2026-119977 to its KEV catalog after attackers began targeting the upgrade-process race condition, which can enable remote code execution during full-package updates. Organizations should update to WordPress 7.1.4 immediately.

  • CISA added the actively exploited high-severity WordPress Core vulnerability CVE-2026-119977 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog.
  • The flaw is a race condition in the WordPress upgrade process that can allow unauthenticated remote attackers to execute code on a server during full-package core upgrades.
  • WordPress released version 7.1.4 on October 28 with patches for CVE-2026-119977 and recommended that sites update immediately.
  • CISA ordered U.S. Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies to secure affected systems by Friday under Binding Operational Directive 26-04.
  • Wordfence reported blocking 13,095 attacks targeting CVE-2026-119977 in the preceding 24 hours.

Technologies: cms

Products: wordpress-core

Vendors: wordpress, wordfence, cisa

Zyxel fixes zero-day exploited to hack nearly 1,000 network switches — Must Read

Zyxel patched CVE-2026-107441, an actively exploited unauthenticated remote-code-execution zero-day in GS1900 network switches that attackers used to compromise nearly 1,000 devices and steal configurations and credentials. Administrators should install the October 22 firmware updates, as earlier patches for CVE-2026-7273 did not stop this separate flaw.

  • Zyxel released firmware updates on October 22 for CVE-2026-107441, an out-of-bounds write flaw in GS1900 switch web interfaces that permits unauthenticated command execution through crafted HTTP requests.
  • GreyNoise observed the Kapibala threat actor compromising 996 Zyxel devices across 48 countries beginning around August 17, 2026, and stealing configurations, hashed root credentials, and network information.
  • The activity was initially attributed to CVE-2026-7273, but Binarly determined that the recovered exploit targeted the separate, previously unknown CVE-2026-107441 flaw.
  • Binarly found that the exploit remained effective against all ten GS1900 firmware releases that had been patched for CVE-2026-7273.
  • Zyxel's updated firmware limits HTTP parameter sizes and validates parameter counts before copying data into memory to prevent the observed exploitation technique.

Technologies: switch

Products: zyxel-gs1900

Vendors: zyxel, binarly, greynoise

APT29-Linked Hackers Hijack Web Analytics Script to Deliver iOS and Android Exploits — Must Read

APT29-linked operators compromised websites, lookalike domains, and Plerdy’s analytics script to silently deliver DarkSword iOS and AndroSnitch Android exploit chains to visitors. The campaign can steal browser data, Wi‑Fi credentials, and—in some iOS cases—extensive device data, underscoring the risk of unpatched mobile browsers and operating systems.

  • Sekoia attributed the Poisoned Source watering-hole campaign to the Russia-linked APT29 group and said it targeted iOS and Android users through compromised sites, lookalike domains, and a compromised Plerdy SEO Tracker script.
  • The injected JavaScript profiled visitors’ browsers and devices before delivering platform-specific exploit chains for iOS or Android.
  • The iOS DarkSword chain could steal browser cookies or, for some iOS 18.5 devices, collect extensive data including messages, contacts, photos, call history, Wi-Fi passwords, and data from several Apple services and apps.
  • The Android chain used CVE-2026-3910 and CVE-2025-27038 to deliver AndroSnitch, which collected Chrome data and Wi-Fi passwords without establishing persistence.

Technologies: mobile-os, browser

Products: ios, android, chrome, plerdy-seo-tracker

Vendors: apple, google, plerdy

Critical Rails Flaw Lets Attackers Write Server Files via Crafted ImageMagick Uploads — Must Read

Rails apps using Active Storage with ImageMagick may let unauthenticated attackers write arbitrary server files—and, with Disk storage, read secrets—through crafted uploads. Upgrade to Rails 8.1.4.1 or 8.0.5.2, ensure MiniMagick 5.1+ and the new ImageMagick policy are active, and rotate potentially exposed secrets.

  • Ruby on Rails disclosed a critical Active Storage flaw that can allow unauthenticated attackers to write arbitrary files through crafted uploads processed by ImageMagick.
  • Applications using Active Storage’s Disk service may also allow attackers to read files accessible to the application process, including secret_key_base and credentials.
  • The issue affects applications that accept untrusted uploads, use MiniMagick for Active Storage image processing, and do not have an ImageMagick policy that blocks the relevant file handlers.
  • Rails fixed the flaw in versions 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2 by shipping an ImageMagick security policy that blocks the MSL handler and other risky functionality.
  • Rails recommends affected users upgrade promptly, confirm the new policy is loaded, and rotate secrets accessible to apps using the Disk service.

Products: ruby-on-rails, active-storage, imagemagick, minimagick, graphicsmagick, ffmpeg

Vendors: rails, imagemagick, minimagick, ffmpeg

Debian and Ubuntu APT Flaw Lets MitM Attackers Swap Verified Packages and Run Code as Root — Must Read

A critical APT flaw (CVE-2026-109518) lets man-in-the-middle attackers who can alter HTTP package traffic use retry behavior to substitute a malicious package that executes as root. Debian and Ubuntu have released or are rolling out fixes, and systems using APT retries should update promptly.

  • It says enforcement should span multiple locations, including native platform hooks, API-level controls, the MCP layer, browsers, and endpoints, and should support responses beyond blocking.
  • The article recommends first building continuous agent discovery, ownership, posture management, and contextual risk tiering before relying on broad inline runtime enforcement.

Binance says fake job interview led to $6.3 billion crypto heist — Must Read

Binance says North Korean Lazarus/TraderTraitor hackers stole about $6.34 billion after luring an engineer through a fake job interview into running malware that compromised wallet infrastructure. The exchange has rebuilt affected systems and says roughly $2.85 billion was frozen or intercepted.

  • Binance said North Korean hackers stole about $6.34 billion in digital assets after compromising its wallet infrastructure.
  • The intrusion began when a Binance software engineer was deceived by a fake recruiter and downloaded a coding assignment containing previously unseen malware.
  • Binance said the malware replaced the legitimate Homebrew pyenv executable on the engineer’s Mac to run commands from an attacker-controlled server.
  • By October 20, the attackers had used the compromised engineer’s computer and an internal AI tool to compromise two additional wallet-infrastructure employees and obtain credentials and a container deployment token.
  • Binance said it rebuilt affected systems, replaced compromised devices, revoked stolen credentials, and that about $2.85 billion of stolen assets had been frozen or intercepted as of November 3.

Products: binance-exchange, homebrew, pyenv

Vendors: binance, homebrew, pyenv

Hackers hijack cPGuard autoupdate to deploy backdoor, steal data — Should Read

Attackers hijacked OpsShield’s cPGuard update channel using compromised credentials, distributing a backdoor and data-stealing script to nearly 3,000 Linux servers. Administrators should update to cPGuard 5.88.25 or later and immediately rotate passwords, database credentials, cloud secrets, and SSH keys.

  • An attacker used compromised credentials to access OpsShield’s cPGuard update distribution infrastructure on November 2, 2026, and distributed a malicious script through the update channel.
  • The compromised cPGuard versions were 5.88.12 through 5.88.19, and OpsShield said it stopped the malicious distribution within 12 hours.
  • The malicious script targeted Linux password hashes, root database configuration, root shell history, and root SSH authorization and known-host files.
  • OpsShield said the stolen data was uploaded through a compromised account to its licensing server, and its investigation indicated the threat actor retrieved 32 files from each customer.
  • OpsShield said 2,946 servers were affected and advised administrators to update to cPGuard 5.88.25 or later and rotate potentially exposed credentials.

Technologies: firewall, antivirus

Products: cpguard

Vendors: opsshield

Google dismantles massive botnet hidden in Android TV boxes — Should Read

Google, Japanese law enforcement, and cybersecurity firms disrupted the X.CPE botnet, which was preinstalled in more than 1.3 million Android TV boxes and other IoT devices allegedly tied to Chinese OEM Videostrong. The malware turned devices into residential proxies and enabled ad fraud, data theft, and installation of additional payloads.

  • Google, Japanese law enforcement, and cybersecurity firms disrupted the X.CPE botnet, which affected more than 1.3 million devices in over 200 countries.
  • Google linked the operation to Chinese Android OEM Videostrong Technology and said it cut ties with the company and barred it from making devices with preloaded Google apps.
  • Most affected devices were Android TV set-top boxes, though telehealth devices, karaoke machines, and digital signage devices were also found infected.
  • Google said the preinstalled software enabled a residential proxy network, allowing criminal affiliates to resell bandwidth, conduct ad fraud, steal data, deliver video content, and install additional software.
  • Google said it took legal action to disrupt domains used to control the botnet, which it said effectively rendered the malware benign by severing its communications.

Technologies: mobile-os, iot-device, proxy

Products: android, android-tv

Vendors: google, videostrong-technology

WorkOS says attacker used ARTEX AI to breach internal sales app — Should Read

WorkOS says an attacker used the ARTEX AI offensive-security framework to breach an internal sales application, exposing business contacts, customer account histories, and communication summaries. The company says production services and WorkOS app data were not accessed, and the incident has been contained.

  • WorkOS identified unauthorized access on October 30, 2026, to an internal application used by its sales team.
  • The attacker accessed business contact details, customer account histories, and summaries or excerpts of sales calls, support discussions, and customer Slack conversations.
  • WorkOS said no WorkOS application data or production services were accessed or affected.
  • WorkOS said the attacker used an AI-powered offensive-security framework to automate reconnaissance and exploitation attempts, and founder Michael Grinich identified ARTEX AI as the likely tool.
  • WorkOS disabled external access to the affected application, engaged an independent incident-response firm, and said it would notify affected customers directly.
